2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that SM Shamim Iqbal, Inspector of District Anti-Corruption Bureau, Khulna, being informant, on 20-3-1997 lodged a First Information Report (shortly FIR) with the Khulna Police Station against three persons for misappropriation of Taka 5,39,000 received by the two accused- petitioners for the purpose of carrying on the activities of two Non-Government Organizations (shortly NGO) named Bonochhaya Mahila Kallayan Samity, Khulna and Bonophool, Khulna. They received the money on the recommendation of Sheik Razzak Ali, the former Member of the Parliament (shortly MP) and also the Speaker of the parliament. 

 5. In this process accused-petitioner No. 1 Taslima Khatun Chanda, as the Chairperson of her NGO Bonochhaya, received two cheques for a total amount of Taka 2,50,000 from the office of the DC, Khulna. Similarly accused-petitioner No. 2 Zakia Akhtar, received two cheques for a total amount of Taka 2,89,000 from the office of the DC, Khulna. Both the accused-petitioners encashed the cheques through bank in the account of their respective NGO but none of the two accused-petitioners utilized the government money so received, nor did they submit any document like voucher, Master Roll etc. as evidence of spending the money. Thus the former MP-Cum Speaker, Sheikh Razzak Ali, by abusing his position and power, assisted the two accused-petitioners in getting an amount of Taka 5,39,000 which was misappropriated. 

 7. The case was sent to the Senior Special Judge, Khulna, who took cognizance of the offences. But subsequently the said judge, by the order dated 3-8-2002, allowed an application filed by the Government for withdrawal of the case of the former Speaker Razzak Ali. Thereafter the case was transferred to the Court of Divisional Special Judge, Khulna, for trial. 

 10. Mr SN Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused- petitioners has submitted that the FIR, the charge-sheet other materials on record do not disclose any offence against the accused-petitioners and therefore continuation of the proceedings would be an abuse of the process of Court. Mr Goswami, the learned Advocate has next submitted that the allegations disclosed in the FIR and charge-sheet is against Mrs. Majeda Ali, the Wife of the former Speaker Sheikh Razzak Ali, as the chairperson of the NGO Banaphool and Advisor of the NGO Bono-chhaya, but she has not been sent up in the charge-sheet, and the principal accused Sheikh Razzak Ali has been withdrawn by the government from the prosecution and therefore, the cognizance taken by the learned Senior Special Judge and the entire proceedings have become groundless, and should be quashed for securing the ends of justice. The learned Advocate, has lastly submitted that Banachhaya and Banaphool are registered NGO's for enhancement of social welfare by undertaking voluntary activities the accused-petitioners are not public servants, and therefore, the learned Special Judge has no jurisdiction to try the case under section 406 of the Penal Code. 

 15. The fundamental allegations against the two accused-petitioners are that they have misappropriated certain amount of Government money that was allocated for the development purpose of Khulna-2 constituency. In doing so they were able to obtain recommendation of the then MP for that constituency and also the then Speaker, Sheikh Razzak Ali and ultimately received the money through the DC Office, but they did not utilize the money so received. 

 19. With regard to jurisdiction of the Special Judge, section 5 (1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (shortly the Act, 1958) provides that an offence under section 406 of the Penal Code is triable by a Special Judge as specified in the Schedule to the Act, 1958. The section is quoted below: 

 24. So, evidently they were not public servants as defined in section 2 (b) of the Act, 1958 read with section 21 of the Penal Code. So a Special Judge exercising jurisdiction under the Act, 1958 has no jurisdiction to try an offence under section 406 of the Penal Code, when the accused person not a public servant. 

 25. Next comes the question whether the proceeding in question is liable to be quashed under section 561A of the Code, 1898 particularly in view of the fact that the former Speaker was involved in the case but with-drawn from prosecution. No doubt the former Speaker was a public servant within the meaning of section 2 (b) of the Act, 1958 read with section 21 of the Penal Code. But the moment the said public servant was withdrawn from prosecution, the Special Judge ceased to have any jurisdiction in view of section 5 (1) read with item (b) of the schedule to the Act, 1985, as quoted above, because there is no involvement of any public servant against whom charge could be framed. 

 30. Mrs Nawazesh Ara Begum, the learned Assistant Attorney General referred the case of Qazi Mustaq Ahmed vs Muhammad Ramzan ,(Pakistan CrlJ, Page 1181) (Lahore) in which the Lahore High Court considered quashment of the proceedings of a case instituted against the sole accused being a Revenue employee (Tehsil Patwari) under section 420 and 406 of the Penal Code. The said Court held that the Magistrate holding the trial was not a Special Judge under the Act, 1958 and therefore, had no jurisdiction to try the case, and that the proceeding was void abinitio and liable to be quashed. 

 38. So we hold that the proceeding of the case is before a Court which is quorum non judice in view of section 5(1) read with item No (b) of the schedule to the Act, 1958.
